review.market_summary: 1) A hawkish Fed turn is the main theme. Inflation has beaten forecasts for a third straight month, producer prices jumped 6.5%, the Fed's Collins is talking about "gradual" hikes, and a December hike is now in play. That is lifting the dollar and pushing bond prices down. Stocks are ignoring it so far (SPY +2.6%, QQQ +3.6% over 5 days). That gap is the risk, but trading against an index rally purely on the model's score is a weak bet. 2) Nvidia is in a governance and regulatory crisis: Huang has resigned, the Treasury has given the company 10 days to explain alleged China chip sales, and a spy scandal involves Lutnick. Money is moving out of NVDA (-12.7%) into AMD, AMAT and LRCX (+11–19%), so the 'export controls hurt all chips' idea is being contradicted by prices outside NVDA. 3) Geopolitics: Iran's drone strike on a US base in Bahrain is a real escalation, but oil still fell 1.9% over 5 days. Defense stocks have already rallied about 4–5%, and the Xi-Trump-Putin summit could ease tensions. China's October data missed across the board, but in China bad data tends to raise hopes of more stimulus rather than push stocks lower.
